identity.title: ALMA and IRIS Observations of the Solar Chromosphere. II. Structure and Dynamics of Chromospheric Plages

paper_type_evidence.quote: we composed and analyzed a unique and comprehensive dataset from joint observations with *ALMA*, the *Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph* (*IRIS*; (cite: DePontieu_etal_2014)), and the *Solar Dynamics Observatory*

targets.name: Plage region in leading part of NOAA AR12651

question.value: How do ALMA Band 6 brightness temperatures in chromospheric plage relate to IRIS Mg II, C II and Si IV diagnostics, where does the 1.25 mm emission form, and does it show shock heating?

evidence.quote: We investigate the high degree of similarity between chromospheric plage features observed in *ALMA*/Band6 (at 1.25 mm wavelength) and *IRIS*/Si IV at 1393 Å.

analysis_steps.goal: Build matched IRIS rasters and radiative temperatures

method.value: Match Band6 2 s frames to slit times within ±1 s; Mg II Trad via Planck inversion; Si IV and C II integrated; hot pixels >10 DN/s interpolated

evidence.quote: we match our *ALMA*/Band6 2 s-cadence series by composing “rasters” that match the time of each slit sampling position to within $\pm$1 s.

fitting.value: Double Gaussian for Mg II features

The jumps in T$_b$ are of order 10%-20% increase from a baseline value of $\approx$ 7,500 K (maximum jump at 8,500 K).

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA Band6 emission and Si IV delineate the same upper parts of spicules and dynamic fibrils; Mg II k is weakly or anti-correlated due to absorption.

evidence.quote: We conclude that the apparent anti-correlation or lack of correlation has its origin in Mg II opacity effects in plage structures.

claims.hypothesis: ALMA Band6 forms in the low-to-mid chromosphere and correlates well with Mg II
claims.experiment: Pearson C.C. between ALMA Tb and IRIS observables in cleanly defined plage, with Bifrost comparison
claims.result: C.C. with Mg II 0.49-0.56; highest among Si IV, C II and ALMA
claims.finding: ALMA Band6 forms near Si IV heights, in upper chromosphere of dynamic features

evidence.quote: We also show that *IRIS*/Mg II h and k is not as well correlated with *ALMA*/Band6 as was previously thought

claims.hypothesis: Higher previous correlations come from plage definition
claims.experiment: Include periphery pixels in the plage sample

evidence.quote: including quieter pixels within plage regions may play a significant role in increasing the C.C. from a marginal value (0.56)

claims.hypothesis: ALMA shows shock heating in plage
claims.experiment: Tb time series against λ-t plots
claims.result: 10-20% Tb jumps from 7,500 K, decays 60-120 s

evidence.quote: our work presents indications for the localized heating of the chromospheric plasma in plage regions by shocks

limitations_admitted.value: Model should not be taken as perfect; modeled Band6 Tb is 2,000 K lower than observed

evidence.quote: the distribution of modeled brightness temperatures of *ALMA*/Band6 is lower by 2,000 K as compared to the observations.
